Pet Food Packaging Trends 2025: B2B Guide to Custom Bags & Pouches

Written by Lisa Wu, Sales Manager & Packaging Project AdvisorPublished June 21, 2025Reviewed August 13, 2026

Lisa coordinates B2B packaging specifications, quotations, sampling and production communication with the BestPackFactory team.

The global pet food market surpassed $115 billion in 2024 and continues to grow at 5–7% annually. As consumer spending on pet nutrition increases, the demand for premium, functional, and sustainable custom pet food packaging is accelerating. This guide covers the top trends B2B buyers should know when sourcing custom pet food bags and pouches in 2025.

1. Premiumization: Pet Food Packaging Goes Upscale

Pet owners are increasingly treating pets as family members — and they expect packaging that reflects premium product quality. Key premiumization trends:

  • Soft-touch matte lamination: Creates a tactile, luxurious feel that commands shelf premium
  • Spot UV on logos and icons: Creates contrast between matte and gloss areas
  • Metallic foil accents: Gold or silver hot foil stamping signals quality
  • Photography-quality photographic print: High-resolution pet and ingredient imagery on bag front
  • Extended panel design: Full-wrap printing that uses the entire bag surface including the bottom gusset

3. Functional Packaging Features in High Demand

B2B buyers sourcing pet food packaging in 2025 should specify these functional features:

  • Resealable zipper: Essential for dry food bags. Press-to-close or slider options.
  • Easy tear notch: First-open convenience, especially for wet food pouches
  • Large format bags (10kg / 20kg): Growing segment for premium kibble and raw food brands
  • Stand-up bottom gusset: Flat bottom for maximum shelf stability and billboarding
  • Oxygen barrier: Multi-layer foil laminate to extend shelf life 12–24 months

4. Regulatory Compliance for Pet Food Packaging

Pet food packaging must comply with food contact material regulations in the target market:

  • USA: FDA 21 CFR (food contact materials)
  • EU: Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 and 10/2011 for plastic food contact
  • UK: UK Food Contact Regulations (post-Brexit)
  • China: GB 4806 series for food contact plastic

Barrier and seal verification method

Method for Pet Food Packaging Trends 2025: B2B Guide to Custom Bags & Pouches: Specify the final laminate, specimen count, conditioning, temperature and humidity, test method, equipment, units and acceptance limits before comparing barrier or seal results.

  • ISO 2528:2017 specifies a gravimetric method for water-vapour transmission rate and states important sensitivity and material limits for that method.
  • ASTM F88/F88M-23 measures flexible-barrier seal strength and requires the support technique to remain consistent within a test series.

Evidence limit: A material name or generic target is not a batch result. Buyers should require a report for the final printed laminate that identifies the method, conditions, specimen preparation, results and acceptance limit.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

The structural trend in pet food packaging is more stand-up and flat-bottom formats with stronger seals, not just new graphics. Factory capabilities that match the trend: flat bottom pouch, quad seal bag and stand-up pouch with handle hole, laminates of PET 12µm / VMPET 12µm / PE 100–130µm or PET 12µm / AL 7µm / PE 110µm for high-fat recipes, seal strength ≥ 45 N / 15 mm, heavy-duty zipper 8–12 mm with slider option for 2 kg+ bags, and a 1.0 m six-face drop test. Matte and anti-scratch finishes keep bags shelf-ready through handling.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which bag formats are trending for pet food?

Flat bottom pouches, quad seal bags and stand-up pouches with handle holes are the dominant formats, all with heavier seals.

What seal strength is expected today?

Buyers now spec ≥ 45 N / 15 mm for pet food bags, up from standard snack levels, because fills are heavier.
